title: Autobiography of a Yogi
author: Paramhansa Yogananda
edition_cited: First edition text (New York: Philosophical Library, 1946) as transcribed by Project Gutenberg, eBook #7452
tradition: Kriya Yoga (Lahiri Mahasaya, Sri Yukteswar lineage)
locator_hints: Chapter 1 (file lines c. 605-620): childhood vision, 'What is behind the darkness of closed eyes?' and 'An immense flash of light at once manifested to my inward gaze'
Chapter 4 (file lines c. 1838-1850, footnote FN4-7 at c. 1905): Lahiri Mahasaya touches blind Ramu between the eyebrows, tells him to hold the mind there and chant for seven days
Chapter 15, footnote FN15-5 (file lines c. 6930-6938): 'During deep meditation, the single or spiritual eye becomes visible within the central part of the forehead'

Chapter 31 (file lines c. 11580-11590): Lahiri Mahasaya 'touched my forehead. Masses of whirling light appeared; the radiance gradually formed itself into the opal-blue spiritual eye, ringed in gold and centered with a white pentagonal star' and the instruction to penetrate through the star
Chapter 14 'An Experience in Cosmic Consciousness' (file lines c. 6155-6480): Sri Yukteswar's touch over the heart and the open-eyed luminous vision
Chapter 26 'The Science of Kriya Yoga' (c. 9887 ff.) and chapter 39/40 footnotes on kutastha (c. 15208-15220)
Chapter 30 (c. 11140-11152): 'the divine eye in the forehead (east)'
summary: The 1946 first edition, public domain, is the lineage's most detailed openly published testimony on the 'spiritual eye'. Yogananda describes its form as seen at the forehead in deep meditation: a field of whirling light that settles into an opal-blue disc ringed in gold with a white five-pointed star at the centre, through which the meditator is told to pass. The book gives no technique for producing it; the Kriya method itself is withheld as initiatory. What it does report repeatedly is onset by a guru's touch: Lahiri Mahasaya touching a disciple's forehead and the light appearing at once, the instruction to a blind disciple to hold attention between the eyebrows with a chanted name for seven days, and Sri Yukteswar's touch producing an open-eyed vision in which the surroundings turn luminous. A childhood episode records a spontaneous flash of light and miniature figures on a 'screen of radiance' behind closed eyes.
why_relevant: First-person and reported testimony about a specific, stable seen light (the tri-coloured spiritual eye) with the conditions of onset, which here are concentration at the brow point and transmission by touch.

date_evidence.basis: Project Gutenberg eBook #7452 (released 2005) transcribes the 1946 Philosophical Library first edition, which Gutenberg distributes as public domain in the US

notes: Later SRF editions revise the text; cite this edition only. Practical instructions for seeing the spiritual eye (gaze lifted to the brow point; 'jyoti mudra', the Kriya form of the six-gate closure) are in SRF lessons and Kriyananda's books, which are in copyright and were not obtainable: see the citation_only records. Many 'lights' in the book are narrative miracle reports; the reading agent should separate those from meditation testimony.
